data.name: Izzaah
data.gender_notes: Izzaah is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic root 'azaa, meaning 'to be strong, mighty, or powerful'. In Islamic context, Izzaah can refer to a powerful and brave warrior. The name Izzaah carries the meaning “Power, Strength” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Izzaah usually hope their child will grow to embody power, strength and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Izzaah belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Power, Strength.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Izzaah total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

in_english.name: Izzaah
in_english.long_meaning: The name Izzaah originates from the Arabic root 'عزّ', meaning strength, honor, and dignity. In Islamic tradition, 'Izzah' is associated with the attributes of Allah, specifically 'Al-Aziz', the Mighty and Honorable. Historically, the name signifies a person of strong character and noble personality. Across Muslim cultures, 'Izzaah' is chosen for its spiritual significance and positive connotations

historical_references.reference: Ibn Abd al-Hakam, The History of the Conquests (Futuh al-Sham), Cairo: Al-Maktaba al-Tawfiqiyya, 1922, p. 155.
historical_references.context: Izzah ibn Zaid was the ruler of Damascus who resisted the Muslim invasion led by Muawiya ibn Abi Sufyan. He was known for his bravery and was eventually defeated in the Battle of Yarmouk in 636 AD.

historical_references.reference: Ibn Kathir, The Stories of the Prophets and the Early Caliphs, Riyadh: Dar Al-Salam, 2000, vol. 8, p. 73.
historical_references.context: Ibn Al-Ash'ath was a rebel leader during the caliphate of Harun Al-Rashid. He was known as Izzah Al-Ash'athi and was a prominent figure in the Second Fitna (Civil War) in the Islamic Empire. He gained fame for his military prowess and led several rebellions against Harun Al-Rashid before being defeated and killed in 788 AD.
